key: Each gets what it desires, but the great state must learn to abase itself.
s: Closing a chapter on states that win one another by lowliness, the verse turns to the greater; Wang Bi, on chapter 61, reads it as a small state stooping only to keep itself whole, while all under heaven turns to a great state that stoops.
src: Wang Bi, Laozi zhu, chapter 61, zh.wikisource (the Huating Zhang edition), revision 2354026 (2024)

opened.locator: chapter 61, comment on 夫兩者各得其所欲，大者宜為下
opened.edition: zh.wikisource 道德經 (王弼本), 華亭張氏 edition, revision 2354026

evidence.words: 小國修下自全而已，不能令天下歸之，大國修下則天下歸之。故曰，各得其所欲，則大者宜為下也。
evidence.gloss: A small state that cultivates lowliness only keeps itself whole and cannot make all under heaven turn to it; a great state that cultivates lowliness has all under heaven turn to it. Hence: each gets what it desires, and the great one should be the lower.
